subject: Post-demo: SLOs & customer-led load test (k6/Locust coordination)
messages:
From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
To: Timothy Chen <tim.chen@skytide.io>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>, Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.ai>, Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 2 Mar 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo: SLOs & customer-led load test (k6/Locust coordination)

Hey Tim / Aisha — great demo earlier, thank you for the time. Per our call I wanted to recap the performance targets we discussed and propose a concrete plan for the customer-led load test so we can validate SLOs before pilot. High level: 

- Latency SLOs: 95th percentile generation latency <= 300ms for short prompts (<=128 tokens); 95th <= 900ms for long prompts (~1k tokens) in best-effort mode.
- Throughput/concurrency: target sustained throughput of ~1.5k tokens/sec (combined across the session) with peak concurrency up to 400 concurrent request streams.
- Streaming: you need low-latency chunked streaming (server-sent events) for assistant use-cases; we agreed to validate partial-token latencies by streaming to a first-byte SLA of <= 120ms for short prompts under 100concurrency.

Next steps I propose:
1) Customer-led load test window: Wed 2026-03-04 09:00–12:00 PT (you suggested morning PT). Confirm?
2) We’ll provide a Redwood test account and a k6 script (attached draft) that mirrors the demo traffic profile; your infra team can run it from their runner or we can provide a managed runner.
3) IP allowlist: we need your team to allowlist the Redwood test runner IPs (we will share CIDRs).
4) Test data and throttles: we’ll use synthetic prompt sets. No production data required.

I attached a first-pass k6 script and a short PDF with test-account setup instructions. Dev — can you spin up the test account and provide the minimal API key (scoped to test) + the IP CIDRs by EOD tomorrow? Mina, please confirm there are no outstanding compliance blockers for a limited test account and note any audit logging footprint we should enable.

Tim / Aisha — please reply with: (a) confirmation of the Wed window, (b) whether you’ll run the script from your runner or want Redwood to run, and (c) who on your infra team will do IP allowlisting so we can sync IPs.

Thanks — Aditya

-- 
Aditya Rao

From: Timothy Chen <tim.chen@skytide.io>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
Cc: Aisha Kaur <aisha.kaur@skytide.io>
Date: Tue, 3 Mar 2026 09:21:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo: SLOs & customer-led load test (k6/Locust coordination)

Thanks Aditya — Wed morning PT works for us, please pencil in 09:00–12:00 PT. Aisha (ops) and I will run the test from our AWS runners; we prefer to keep the traffic originating from our network so our monitoring captures end-to-end behavior. A few quick notes/asks: 

- IP allowlist: our security team needs the exact IPs/CIDRs at least 24 hours before the run.
- Test account: we need a test API key with request-scoped limits and clear expiry; we will not use production keys.
- Metrics: we’ll push k6 metrics to our DataDog. Would be great if Redwood can emit the per-token latency histogram and a streaming-first-byte marker to the same push endpoint (or share the raw logs).
- Ramp profile: we’ll run two passes — a ramp to 200 concurrency over 10 minutes, hold 30 minutes, then ramp to 400 concurrency over 15 minutes and hold 45 minutes.

We’ll attach our contact details for allowlisting: ops@skytide.io and the infra owner is Aisha (cc’d). See you Wed.

—Tim
From: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
Cc: Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.ai>, Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 3 Mar 2026 11:45:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Post-demo: SLOs & customer-led load test (k6/Locust coordination)

Aditya — done. I created a scoped test account and a single-use API key; details below (do not paste into any external doc):

- Test account id: skt-test-2026-03-aditya
- API key: redacted (will deliver to Tim via encrypted channel per Mina)
- Expiry: 2026-03-05T23:59:59Z

IP CIDRs to allowlist (these are our managed test runners for external customer-originated runs):
- 18.205.40.0/22
- 52.203.0.0/18
- 3.208.192.0/20

Attached a cleaned-up k6 script (k6-loadscript_v1.js) with the ramp profile Tim requested and an example SSE/streaming check that records first-byte latency as an event. Notes for execution:
- Default VU (virtual users) profile maps to your ramp; the script emits per-request tags so Redwood traces can align with your DataDog metrics.
- For Locust teams: equivalent steps are called out in header comments; we recommend k6 for this pass because of easier CI runners, but Locust is fine if you need Python-based hooks.

Mina — I left the audit_log flag ON for this test account; you said that would be sufficient. Ping if you need extra context for SOC/ISO evidence.

—Dev

Attachment: k6-loadscript_v1.js
From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>

Date: Thu, 4 Mar 2026 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo: SLOs & customer-led load test (k6/Locust coordination) — final checklist

Thanks Tim/Aisha — confirmed for Wed 2026-03-04 09:00–12:00 PT (we’re aligned on run origin from your runners). Final checklist before we start: 

- Redwood will deliver: scoped test API key (Dev — already created), k6 script and example Locust notes (attached), and a small README with expected metric names and log keys.
- Customer will: run the k6 script from their runner, allowlist the Redwood CIDRs listed by Dev, and configure DataDog to accept k6 telemetry.
- Mina: audit logging will be retained for 90 days for the test account and we’ll export the minimal set of request traces you requested. Confirmed?
- Tim: please share the run contact phone number for the Wed window and the slack handle so we can coordinate live.

If everything above is green, we’ll be standing by in the run window and will collect: per-request latencies, streaming-first-byte times, error rates, and token throughput. After the run we’ll schedule a 60-min post-mortem to review results and make any necessary model/runtime tuning recommendations.

Looking forward — see you tomorrow morning.

Best,
Aditya
